done.issue: major, rps7200/shortcuts.py:209 (FR-14 was only partly fixed: <Control-s> and <Control-Key-s> are one Tk pattern but were compared as different strings)
done.change: Confirmed. I added shortcuts.canonical(), which gives each key the spelling sequence_for writes: Key/KeyPress are folded, Key- is dropped for _NAMED keys, and modifiers go in a fixed order. Shift is kept where it is written. A release, a button or an unknown modifier comes back unchanged. conflicts() groups by the canonical form, and resolve() compares canonical forms against the shipped key. I chose to compare in canonical form rather than store it, so what is stored stays the operator's own spelling, and a key Tk refuses (the <Foo> test) is still reported as written. The shortcut editor's _ShortcutSettings._set in tools/gui.py had the same hole the other way round: a captured <Control-Key-s> against a hand-written <Control-s>. It now looks the key up in canonical form too. New tests: test_another_spelling_of_a_taken_key_is_the_same_key (flip=<ACCEL-s> is reverted, and so are <Key-F5> and <F5> on two actions), test_a_key_respelt_as_its_own_default_is_its_own, test_a_key_has_one_spelling (parametrised), test_every_shipped_key_is_already_in_its_one_spelling, and in test_gui test_the_editor_refuses_a_key_held_under_another_spelling. Checked: with the old comparison, both the shortcuts test and the gui test fail. Commit bcab57b.
